label: Midnight Office (Mesoniktikon)
description: The Byzantine Midnight Office (Mesoniktikon), appointed for the midnight hour. UNABHOR1997 gives three genuinely distinct day-forms -- Weekday, Saturday, and Sunday -- differing in their psalmody, closing prayers, and (on Sunday) a real Canon to the Holy Trinity in place of the Weekday/Saturday Kathisma and its prayers (Finding M0). The correct day-form is resolved from the date. Full festal and Lenten variations, and the Octoechos-dependent Canon to the Holy Trinity and Hypakoe of the Tone on Sunday, are deferred beyond this baseline.

sections.label: Opening
sections.notes: The Usual Beginning, including the risen-from-sleep troparia and two opening prayers, shared word-for-word between the Weekday and Saturday forms (UNABHOR1997 pp.1-2/21-22).

items.text: The Priest blesses: Blessed is our God, always, now and ever and unto ages of ages.

sections.label: Opening
sections.notes: The Sunday form's own, shorter opening -- no troparia, no opening prayers (UNABHOR1997 pp.40-41).

items.text: The Priest blesses: Blessed is our God, always, now and ever and unto ages of ages.

sections.label: Psalm 50
sections.notes: Psalm 50 (LXX), shared by all three day-forms.

items.label: Psalm 50 (LXX) — Have mercy on me, O God

sections.label: Prayers I-IX, and the Final Morning Prayer
sections.notes: Finding M2: nine Prayers of St. Macarius the Great / St. Basil the Great / to the Theotokos / to Christ / to the Guardian Angel, plus the Final Morning Prayer -- all missing entirely before this fix. Weekday and Saturday only; Sunday's own shorter opening has none of these (UNABHOR1997 pp.2-7/22-27).

items.label: Prayers I-IX, and the Final Morning Prayer

sections.label: The Seventeenth Kathisma
sections.notes: Psalm 118 (LXX) in full, in three stases -- the Weekday form's own appointed Kathisma (Finding M1: this is NOT preceded by a separate 'Psalm 117,' which does not exist in the real office).

items.label: Psalm 118 (LXX) — Blessed are the undefiled in the way

sections.label: The Ninth Kathisma
sections.notes: Psalms 64-69 (LXX) -- the Saturday form's own appointed Kathisma, entirely different from the Weekday form's Seventeenth Kathisma (Finding M0).

sections.label: The Symbol of Faith, and Troparia
sections.notes: The Creed, then the Weekday form's own troparia -- the Bridegroom/Ten Virgins theme, Tone 8 (Finding M3, corrected: not a Canon of Odes; the 'wise virgins' phrase in the finding's own wording is from an unrelated opening prayer, not this troparia set, though this set does share the same theme).

sections.label: The Symbol of Faith, and Troparia
sections.notes: The Creed, then the Saturday form's own troparia -- Trinity-praise themed, Tone 2, structurally distinct from the Weekday form's Bridegroom troparia (Finding M0).

sections.label: The Canon to the Holy Trinity
sections.notes: The Sunday form's own centerpiece, immediately after Psalm 50 -- a real Canon to the Most Holy Trinity (tone-dependent, Octoechos-sourced, disclosed as deferred rather than fabricated) followed by the fixed Hymns to the Trinity of Gregory the Sinaite (built in full).

items.label: The Canon to the Most Holy Trinity
Hymns to the Trinity, by Gregory the Sinaite

sections.label: Lord, Have Mercy (Forty Times), the Prayer of the Hours, and the Blessing
sections.notes: Finding M3 (confirmed real, further along in the sequence than first read): Lord, have mercy (forty times) with the Prayer of the Hours, then More Honourable and the priest's blessing.

items.label: Lord, Have Mercy (Forty Times), the Prayer of the Hours, and the Blessing

sections.label: The Repeated Trisagion, Hypakoe, Lord Have Mercy, and the Blessing
sections.notes: Sunday's own version of this position: the repeated Trisagion, the Hypakoe of the Tone (tone-dependent, Octoechos-sourced, disclosed as deferred), then Lord-have-mercy-forty (bare, with no Prayer of the Hours on this day-form), More Honourable, and the blessing.

items.label: Lord, Have Mercy (Forty Times), and the Blessing

sections.label: Prayer to the Holy Trinity
sections.notes: The brief Trinity prayer shared with Saturday (and, in different wording, with the Third Hour's own closing elsewhere in this corpus).

sections.label: Prayer to the Holy Trinity, and the Prayer of St. Eustratius
sections.notes: The same brief Trinity prayer as the Weekday form, followed by the Saturday form's own Prayer of St. Eustratius (Finding M0 -- Saturday-specific content, fitting for the day traditionally kept for the departed).

sections.label: Psalms 120 and 133, the Repeated Trisagion, and the Memorial Troparia
sections.notes: Finding M3 (confirmed real): a second 'O come, let us worship,' then Psalms 120 and 133, the repeated Trisagion, two sets of memorial troparia for the departed (with their own Kontakion, Theotokia, and an intervening prayer), the litany for protection from calamity, and the real dismissal -- previously represented by nothing but a single generic closing rubric.

items.text:
Come, let us worship God our King.
Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ our King and God.
Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ Himself, our King and our God. And three reverences.

items.label: Psalm 120 (LXX) — I have lifted up mine eyes to the mountains
Psalm 133 (LXX) — Behold now, bless ye the Lord
Lord, Have Mercy (Twelve Times), and This Prayer

sections.label: Prayer to the Most Holy Trinity
sections.notes: The Sunday form's own closing prayer, a composition of Mark the Monk -- Sunday has no Kathisma, no Psalms 120/133, and no memorial troparia at this position; it proceeds directly from this prayer to its own dismissal.

items.label: Prayer to the Most Holy Trinity (a composition of Mark the Monk)

sections.label: The Dismissal
sections.notes: Sunday's own dismissal, naming the Resurrection explicitly -- no calamity litany precedes it on this day-form.

sections.label: Mutual Forgiveness, the Ectenia, and Veneration of the Icons
sections.notes: Shared verbatim by all three day-forms: mutual bows and forgiveness, a closing Ectenia for the Church and the monastic community, and veneration of the icons.
